question: A 33-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of dry cough and low-grade fever. Four months ago, she was diagnosed with major depressive disorder and started treatment with fluoxetine. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A diagnosis of upper respiratory infection is made and a medication is prescribed to relieve her symptoms. A drug with which of the following mechanisms of action should be avoided in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fluoxetine is an SSRI" -> "increases serotonin levels" -> "can lead to serotonin syndrome" -> "certain medications can exacerbate serotonin syndrome" -> "inhibition of NMDA glutamate receptors can increase serotonin activity" -> "should be avoided in this patient" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has major depressive disorder" -> "treated with fluoxetine" -> "risk of drug interactions" -> "some medications can increase side effects" -> "stimulation of α-adrenergic receptors can cause increased anxiety" -> "should be avoided in this patient" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has upper respiratory infection" -> "medications can relieve symptoms" -> "some mechanisms can worsen existing conditions" -> "reduction in secretion viscosity may not be effective" -> "unclear if it poses a risk" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Dry cough and low-grade fever present" -> "symptomatic treatment is needed" -> "inhibition of H1 receptors can help with cough" -> "not contraindicated" -> "should be considered" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Fluoxetine can interact with other medications" -> "certain mechanisms can lead to adverse effects" -> "disruption of mucoid disulfide bonds may not be relevant" -> "unclear if it poses a risk" -> 65%
analysis: The patient is being treated with fluoxetine, which is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). SSRIs can increase the risk of serotonin syndrome, especially when combined with other medications that affect serotonin levels. Among the options provided, 'Inhibition of NMDA glutamate receptors' (option opd) is relevant because certain NMDA antagonists can potentially interact with SSRIs and increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. Therefore, this mechanism of action should be avoided in this patient.
